_doc: Profile pictures (#189). `GET /api/auth/me` and every administrator user object (auth/admin-users.json) carry `avatarUrl`: the path of the user's picture, or null. The path names the 256 px square; the same path with `?size=64` is the 64 px square, and a client picks the file by the size it draws times the device pixel ratio (the web: `avatarSrc`, 64 px up to 64 device pixels). A new picture has a new path (it ends in a content hash), so a cached file is never stale. The files need a session like every other route (send the bearer token; an `` without it gets a 401), any signed-in user of the server may read any user's picture, and the answer is `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` (revalidate with the ETag each time), `Content-Type: image/jpeg`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Upload: `POST /api/account/avatar`, multipart/form-data with the picture in the field `file`, a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 5 MB, at most 25 megapixels and 8192 px a side, not animated; the type is judged by the content, never the file name. The server decodes it and stores two fresh square JPEGs (the centre square of anything that is not square), so EXIF (camera, GPS), XMP, ICC profiles and text chunks are never kept or served. 10 uploads per user and hour (429 rate_limited, Retry-After). `DELETE /api/account/avatar` removes your own (204, also when there is none). An administrator removes anyone's with `DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}/avatar` (204; 404 when the user has none; audited as `avatar_removed`; no re-authentication). Access tokens cannot use any of these routes. The picture is removed with the account, is in personal backups (`account/avatar.jpg`, backup/README.md) and in server backups.
